analysis: Kickoff update (7:25pm ET, post-inactives). Carolina is thinner than it was this afternoon: WR Jalen Coker and RG Damien Lewis are inactive on top of WR Xavier Legette and both starting corners (Horn, Mike Jackson) on IR, leaving Tetairoa McMillan as the only established receiver. Detroit is close to full strength (only G Ben Bartch out; CB D.J. Reed active). With those absences priced, the sim makes Detroit a 7.3-point favorite against a -3.5 market -- but the betting split pushes back: Detroit has 75% of spread tickets and only 52% of the money, meaning the bigger bets are on Carolina +3.5.

The total sits at 50.5 with the over juiced to -122 after touching 51.5, and the public has now piled in (roughly 80% of bets and money on the over). The case for points is intact -- Detroit has scored exactly 31 in all three games and allowed a league-high 898 passing yards, and Carolina has lost both starting corners -- but at -122 the over needs to win 55% of the time, and Carolina losing two receivers trims its own scoring side. That makes the over a smaller play than it was at -110 this afternoon; 51.5 at -110 is the better ticket if available.
